title: LAN, WAN and Packet Switching
welcome_lead: Shrink networks to a building or stretch them globally with packet switching.
meta_desc: IBDP CS adventure on LAN vs WAN, packet switching and routing fundamentals.
final_note: Packets find their own path - resilient and efficient!

concepts.def: Local Area Network, small geographic scope.
Wide Area Network spanning cities or continents.
Data chunk with header and payload.
Dedicated path reserved for the call.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Wired Ethernet or Wi-Fi over short range.

Switches connect devices; one router links to the WAN.

Large message split into packets, each routed independently.

Reassembled at destination; lost packets retransmitted (TCP).

Router checks destination IP, looks up routing table.

Forwards on next hop's interface; TTL decrements to prevent loops.
